blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: ARPA/DARPA, NSF, universities, telecom incumbents, IBM, Intel, Xerox, Cisco, Microsoft, Apple and standards organizations. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Circuit-switched carrier networks alongside packet-switched research networks; LANs joined through routers and common protocols.
Enterprise hardware, software licensing, leased data services, commercial networking and IT integration.
Packet switching divides traffic into independently forwarded units; TCP/IP enabled interconnection among heterogeneous networks without central ownership.

An office PC sends an Ethernet frame to a switch; a router forwards its IP packet toward a remote network. At each routed hop the link-layer framing may change while the IP-layer delivery objective persists.
Research funding, standards, vendors and carriers jointly enabled interoperable networking. ARPANET was not identical to the modern Internet.
